# Open311 GIS handoff and reviewed dispatch

The GIS desk carries a complete municipal source selection through a practical analyst workflow: import an original collection or service report, prepare a named map and table handoff, exchange editable GIS files, inspect returned proposals, save review decisions, and deliver a mapped dispatch package. The browser, CLI, typed SDK and installed merchant tools use the same saved workspace.

The installed **open311-gis** selection includes municipal source operations, service-performance reporting and this GIS desk. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for packaging and Applications, [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) for the complete browser workflow, [FORMATS.md](FORMATS.md) for GIS and CSV interoperability, and [MCP.md](MCP.md) for the installed merchant tools.

## Source intake and identity

Import either a complete **commons.open311.collection-export.v1** file or a complete **commons.open311.reporting-workspace.v1** package. A reporting JSON export includes its original source closure; choose the saved report when the file contains several reports. The importer checks the original collection/report relationships and keeps the exact UTF-8 file, its hash, the selected original request editions, capture times, source coverage and attribution.

Each feature key derives from the exact frozen endpoint, jurisdiction and service_request_id. A local GeoPackage fid is an ordinary integer row identifier. Source-version hashes include arbitrary original fields, including nested provider extensions. Source status, case-closure notes and internal source review remain visible beside the GIS analyst fields.

A handoff can combine several imported collections and reports. For each feature identity, the latest observed source edition wins, followed by deterministic source-hash/capture/source-ID ordering for a time tie. All original candidate versions remain inspectable from the retained input files. This selection describes the observations present in the imported sources; the captured source window, provider cap, update-feed population and unresolved intervals remain in its coverage.

## Start a desk

Direct modules require Node.js 22.13 or newer. The complete installed merchant runtime requires Node.js 22.16 or newer.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

Open the private URL printed in the compact startup JSON. The selected directory contains open311-gis.sqlite. Source files, analyst uploads, immutable handoff editions, review decisions, dispatches and operation recovery are committed in SQLite transactions. State and head reads use compact saved summaries, so reopening the workbench avoids parsing every historical source body.

In an installed package, use **starforge open311-gis** with the same arguments. Merchant Applications offers **Open311 GIS handoff** and verifies the selected directory, original workspace identity and running server instance.

## Create a complete handoff

Inspect and import the original source:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs inspect-source \
  --file /absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --file /absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json \
  --request-id gis-source-001 --expected-revision 0
~~~

For a report package, add --report with an ID returned by inspect-source. Keep the source ID returned by import. A handoff definition selects that ID and explicit operating defaults:

~~~json
{
  "name": "Municipal GIS allocation",
  "sourceIds": ["SOURCE_ID_FROM_IMPORT"],
  "filters": {
    "q": "",
    "statuses": [],
    "serviceCodes": [],
    "geometry": "any"
  },
  "defaults": {
    "assignedTeam": "",
    "assetId": "",
    "workOrderId": "",
    "priority": "",
    "action": "review",
    "dueDate": "",
    "note": ""
  }
}
~~~

Save that definition through the browser or as a JSON file, then run:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs handoff \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --file /absolute/handover/gis-definition.json \
  --request-id gis-handoff-001 --expected-revision 1
~~~

The returned handoff ID selects complete exports:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --handoff HANDOFF_ID --kind gpkg \
  --out /absolute/handover/municipal-analyst.gpkg
~~~

The same selection supports geojson, csv, json and html. The browser map and table show a searchable page, while each export contains the complete saved handoff. The GeoPackage also includes the original imported source files, handoff metadata and coverage as registered attribute tables.

## Analyst edits and returned files

The editable fields are geometry, assigned_team, asset_id, work_order_id, priority, action, due_date and analyst_note. Geometry is an RFC 7946 WGS84 Point or NULL. Action is review, dispatch, defer or dismiss. Due dates use YYYY-MM-DD or an empty value.

Open the GeoPackage's open311_features layer in the GIS editor, inspect the retained source columns and add the allocation or location changes. Keep feature_key, handoff_id, handoff_sha256 and source_sha256, along with the other source columns. Save the edited file and import it against its original handoff:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs return \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --handoff HANDOFF_ID --analyst "Municipal GIS analyst" \
  --file /absolute/handover/municipal-analyst-return.gpkg \
  --request-id gis-return-001 --expected-revision CURRENT_REVISION
~~~

GeoJSON, CSV and analyst JSON follow the same flow. The return retains every original byte and shows proposed editable-field changes, unknown or duplicate feature keys, source-column changes, invalid geometry, unchanged rows and missing keys. A missing returned row remains a visible missing entry; historical source records remain in the saved handoff.

Inspect a return with return-show --id RETURN_ID or the browser. A review selection explicitly names the current target handoff, reviewer and individual proposal IDs:

~~~json
{
  "returnId": "RETURN_ID",
  "handoffId": "CURRENT_HANDOFF_ID",
  "reviewer": "Municipal service supervisor",
  "note": "Assignment and location reviewed",
  "accept": ["CHANGE_ID"],
  "reject": []
}
~~~

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs decision \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --file /absolute/handover/gis-decision.json \
  --request-id gis-decision-001 --expected-revision CURRENT_REVISION
~~~

The action saves a decision and a new immutable handoff edition. Accepted proposals must still match their original source version; competing analyst changes produce per-field conflicts with the old, current and proposed values. Other accepted fields can be reviewed in a separate explicit selection. Already decided proposals retain their reviewer and time.

To reverse an accepted analyst change, export the current handoff, edit the desired fields, return that file and save a new review decision. Original proposals and decisions stay available.

## Refresh the original source selection

Import a newer complete source collection or report, then create a handoff with predecessorId set to the current handoff in the same series. Choose the desired source IDs and filters.

An unchanged original source hash carries its accepted analyst fields, geometry and last decision forward. A changed original source version starts with the new handoff defaults and original geometry, records its previous source hash and appears as changed source. This keeps the source refresh and the supervisor's GIS decisions distinguishable. Earlier handoffs, source versions and return files remain available.

## Prepare reviewed dispatch

Dispatch selects rows whose action is dispatch and which have an accepted analyst decision. The definition contains a name, saved handoff ID, actual destination label, optional note and optional row keys. Omit keys to include all reviewed dispatch rows.

~~~json
{
  "name": "Reviewed municipal allocation",
  "handoffId": "REVIEWED_HANDOFF_ID",
  "destination": "Municipal work-order intake",
  "note": "Reviewed allocation for the selected source edition",
  "columns": [
    { "name": "external_case_id", "field": "serviceRequestId" },
    { "name": "responsible_team", "field": "assignedTeam" },
    { "name": "asset_reference", "field": "assetId" },
    { "name": "work_order_reference", "field": "workOrderId" },
    { "name": "longitude", "field": "longitude" },
    { "name": "latitude", "field": "latitude" },
    { "name": "dispatch_note", "field": "note" }
  ]
}
~~~

Save the file with dispatch --file DEFINITION.json and the same revision/request controls. Export its returned dispatch ID with --dispatch ID and kind csv, gpkg, geojson, json or html. The four identity columns are retained in mapped CSV, along with its declared reversible cell encoding. Destination column names are explicit operator mappings. The output remains a saved deliverable associated with the selected handoff, source versions and accepted decisions.

## Complete receiving and recovery

Export kind workspace without an item selection. This file contains the complete GIS source files, historical handoffs, original analyst uploads, decisions, dispatches, received histories and original operation inputs/results.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis --kind workspace \
  --out /absolute/handover/municipal-gis-complete.json

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/gis/cli.mjs receive \
  --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis-received \
  --file /absolute/handover/municipal-gis-complete.json \
  --request-id gis-receive-001 --expected-revision 0
~~~

Receiving checks the original source, file comparisons, accepted decisions, handoff lineage and dispatch derivation before the transaction commits. Each receiving operation stores the exact incoming file hash/byte count and sealed package hash as a compact descriptor; the imported original records and municipal/analyst files transfer once, avoiding recursive package nesting on subsequent handovers. It preserves the original workspace identity and history, then appends the receiving action and revision. Open the receiving directory in the browser or Applications and continue editing its current handoff.

Every mutation uses a stable requestId and an observed expectedRevision. The CLI can create a request ID and read the current revision when those options are omitted; explicit values make automation and recovery clearer. After an uncertain response, query operation --request-id ID and repeat the original action. A new request ID names a new intended action.

Source and analyst imports are limited to 128 MiB; full workspace packages and exports are limited to 256 MiB. A handoff supports 100,000 selected identities. Complete immutable data stays in the workspace and complete exports, while browser and merchant lists are paged. GeoPackage preparation needs writable space in the selected private directory.

## Primary format and provider references

- [OGC GeoPackage 1.4.0](https://www.geopackage.org/spec140/index.html): SQLite header, core tables, SRS declarations and standard binary geometry.
- [RFC 7946](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7946.html): WGS84 GeoJSON longitude/latitude and nullable geometry.
- [QGIS editing documentation](https://docs.qgis.org/3.44/en/docs/user_manual/working_with_vector/editing_geometry_attributes.html): ordinary geometry and attribute editing.
- [Connected Bits](https://connectedbits.com/): municipal CRM, GIS, asset and work-order integrations and supervisor map/list workflows.
- [BOS:311 Open311 access](https://311.boston.gov/open311) and [provider documentation](https://311.boston.gov/open311/docs): original municipal source access and vendor extensions.

Source attribution from each imported connection remains in the GIS files, full receiving package and printable report.

# GIS file interoperability

The GIS desk exports four editable handoff formats and a complete printable report. The immutable original row is retained beside separate analyst fields. A complete GIS workspace JSON also carries every original source file, uploaded analyst file, historical handoff, saved decision and dispatch.

## GeoPackage

The writer uses the [OGC GeoPackage 1.4.0 standard](https://www.geopackage.org/spec140/index.html), implemented through Node's built-in SQLite database. The file has application_id 0x47504B47 and user_version 10400.

| Table | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| gpkg_spatial_ref_sys | Required undefined Cartesian/geographic systems and EPSG:4326 WGS84 |
| gpkg_contents | Registered feature and attribute tables, UTC last-change values and feature extent |
| gpkg_geometry_columns | open311_features.geom as two-dimensional EPSG:4326 POINT |
| open311_features | Integer fid, standard binary Point or SQL NULL, original columns and analyst fields |
| open311_handoff | Complete saved handoff/dispatch metadata, source identity and return binding |
| open311_sources | Complete unchanged imported collection/report texts and their original file hashes |
| open311_coverage | Original collection selections, provider/window coverage and attribution |

Located geometry uses the standard GP header followed by ordinary two-dimensional Point WKB, with X=longitude and Y=latitude. This order follows the GeoPackage requirement even where an authority's general SRS definition lists axes differently. The reader understands little- or big-endian header and WKB independently, with either no envelope or an XY envelope. It accepts the standard empty-Point representation as NULL and preserves unlocated features as ordinary rows.

The source's latitude and longitude must both be finite values within WGS84 bounds. Missing or invalid source coordinates create NULL geometry. The original coordinate values remain in source_latitude/source_longitude and the complete source_json. Top-level original x/y appear literally in source_projected_x/source_projected_y; nested projected attributes remain in source_json. A transform requires an explicitly implemented and selected source-coordinate contract.

Open open311_features in a GIS application that supports GeoPackage feature editing. Preserve its source/identity columns and edit geom plus the analyst columns. The original attribute tables can be inspected alongside the layer. A returned layer must retain the standard source columns and its EPSG:4326 declaration. The importer retains invalid rows as conflicts. A re-export with one renamed compatible layer is accepted when its complete original columns identify it unambiguously.

The reader opens the selected SQLite file read-only with extensions disabled and trusted_schema off. It reads an ordinary feature table and its declared geometry metadata. Source lineage is checked against the saved handoff after decoding.

## GeoJSON

The file is an [RFC 7946 FeatureCollection](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7946.html), with WGS84 Point coordinates [longitude, latitude] or geometry:null. A bbox is present only when the complete selection contains located geometry.

Feature id and feature_key identify the saved source identity. Properties contain the full original source columns and separate analyst fields. The foreign member open311 carries the selected handoff ID/hash, source-file descriptions and original coverage. Edited returns preserve the row identity/source columns. CRS reprojection must be completed explicitly before returning RFC 7946 coordinates.

## Analyst JSON

The schema is commons.open311.gis-analyst.v1. It contains handoffId, handoffSha256, original source/coverage metadata and a rows array. Each row has the same flat original/analyst columns plus a geometry Point or NULL.

This format is convenient for scripted analyst tools. Use the saved original handoff fields and change only geometry or the documented analyst columns. Dispatch JSON instead contains the complete sealed reviewed-dispatch record and source descriptions.

## CSV

CSV uses UTF-8, quoted RFC 4180-style fields, doubled quotes inside quoted values and CRLF record separators. Embedded commas, quotes, Unicode and line breaks remain in their original fields. Point geometry uses longitude and latitude; two empty cells represent NULL. Both coordinate columns are required in an analyst return.

The columns include the original source values, canonical source_json/source_review_json/report_context_json and these editable fields:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| assigned_team | Operator-selected responsible team |
| asset_id | Selected asset reference |
| work_order_id | Selected work-order reference |
| priority | Explicit operator priority text |
| action | review, dispatch, defer or dismiss |
| due_date | A real YYYY-MM-DD date or empty |
| analyst_note | Analyst's operating note |
| longitude / latitude | WGS84 geometry, or two empty cells |

The final open311_csv_encoding column is reserved and contains apostrophe-v1 on every row. Text beginning with an apostrophe, or a spreadsheet formula prefix =, +, -, @ after leading whitespace, is prefixed with one apostrophe when written. The declared decoder removes that one protective prefix when importing. A literal initial apostrophe therefore appears doubled in the raw CSV. This convention keeps exported source text inert in common spreadsheet workflows while preserving an exact reversible representation.

Keep the encoding column when editing this exported CSV. GIS/CSV tools that display the literal protective apostrophe retain it in the returned file; the importer applies the declared decoding. A separately produced unmarked CSV is read literally. Source-field equality is checked after decoding.

Reviewed dispatch CSV uses the selected destination column names, four forced source/handoff identity columns and the same encoding marker. Dispatch column names must be distinct and cannot use any reserved identity/encoding name.

## Returned changes and source geometry

The source_geometry_state describes the original source: SOURCE_POINT, MISSING_COORDINATES or INVALID_COORDINATES. The current geometry and geometryOrigin distinguish a later accepted analyst location from that original state.

Source column changes, duplicate keys, unknown features, missing columns and invalid coordinates remain individual conflicts. Missing rows are listed separately. A returned file can contain both valid proposals and conflicts; a supervisor selects the proposals to decide.

The original returned file bytes remain downloadable through kind returned. This includes invalid structural files retained for review, their errors and the original handoff selection. Current source versions and competing analyst fields are checked again when applying a decision.

## Complete original attribution

Each imported source's publisher, title, license, license URL and source URL are retained. GeoPackage attribute tables and the complete GIS workspace preserve the original collection/report text. HTML includes the original source selection, coverage, attribution, literal status notes and original selected records. The file formats retain those distinctions through subsequent receiving and reopening.

# Install the Open311 GIS operating product

The open311-gis selection includes three applications: **Open311 municipal service operations**, **Open311 service performance**, and **Open311 GIS handoff**. Each operates its own saved directory. Complete collection/report files carry the original source selection into GIS; the GIS receiving package carries the whole editable analyst/review/dispatch workflow to another installation.

## Build one exact source edition

From the selected repository checkout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo . --ref EXACT_GIS_SOURCE_COMMIT \
  --selection open311-gis \
  --out /absolute/new/open311-gis-package --offline
~~~

Choose the exact source revision and a new output directory. The selection includes the maintained release/installation tools, the three Open311 components, the merchant provider contributions and browser assets. The product uses the existing starforge executable. Source modules remain available under package/source.

Direct GIS modules require Node.js 22.13 or newer with built-in SQLite. The complete installed merchant runtime requires Node.js 22.16 or newer, Linux, Python 3.11 or newer and util-linux flock. GeoPackage support uses the built-in SQLite implementation.

The installed exports are:

| Export | API |
| --- | --- |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-gis | Typed source, format, handoff, review, dispatch, workspace and server functions |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-gis/workspace | Durable GIS workspace |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-gis | Original merchant provider |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-gis/client | Typed adapter for the existing merchant callTool transport |

## Prepare the original private runtime

Run these commands from the private directory where the delivered source-only merchant package is installed. Use the original delivered archive and its exact SHA-256:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/handover/ORIGINAL_GIS_ARCHIVE.tgz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install install \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install inspect \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime --load --source
~~~

Wait for READY. The original runtime profile selects the archive's declared dependencies, keeping its source under municipal-runtime/package/source and dependencies under municipal-runtime/node_modules.

Resume an interrupted installation with runtime-install resume --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime. With an existing populated cache, add --offline --cache /absolute/private/npm-cache to install or resume. Offline native-module preparation needs a compiler and Node headers matching the actual selected executable; --node-headers /absolute/private/node-prefix selects a prefix containing include/node.

Run installed commands through this prepared runtime so their source and dependencies remain aligned:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-gis init --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis
~~~

## Acquire or choose complete source files

The existing municipal operations desk exports a complete collection as kind json:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311 export --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-operations \
  --collection COLLECTION_ID --kind json \
  --out /absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json
~~~

A selected service-report JSON export contains its original collection sources and report interpretation:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-reporting export --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-reporting \
  --report REPORT_ID --kind json \
  --out /absolute/handover/municipal-report.json
~~~

Keep the complete source file unchanged. Open the GIS desk's source inspector to select its saved report when a package contains several reports. Imported source windows, unresolved caps, original status notes and attribution remain visible in GIS coverage and exports.

## Open the saved GIS application

After initializing or receiving the GIS directory, start its browser directly:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-gis serve --workspace /absolute/private/municipal-gis \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The compact LISTENING line contains the private URL, original workspace ID, directory binding and server instance. Open that URL to establish its browser session.

For merchant Applications, open the existing runtime workspace with this prepared runtime and choose **Open311 GIS handoff**. Select the same initialized GIS directory. The application provider reads open311-gis.sqlite, binds the selected original workspace ID and verifies the live startup record before opening the browser. The GIS source command and browser assets are declared by the additive open311-gis contribution.

When receiving a complete customer workspace, receive into a new empty GIS directory first, then select that received directory in Applications. The receiver keeps the original workspace identity and adds the receiving action to its history. An already open receiving browser follows the new identity and retains its recovery information by the selected directory.

## Complete the operating workflow

The [browser guide](WORKSPACE.md) covers source inspection, map/table handoff selection, analyst files, returned proposals and conflicts, supervisor decisions, mapped dispatch outputs, exact command recovery and complete workspace receiving.

The [source/API guide](README.md) provides equivalent CLI definitions and examples. The [format guide](FORMATS.md) describes the GeoPackage layers, GeoJSON geometry, immutable source columns and reversible CSV encoding. The [merchant guide](MCP.md) configures original input aliases, initializes the maintained merchant host and operates complete files through the existing retained reader.

A complete GIS handover should include the workspace JSON and the selected human/GIS outputs. The receiving operator can reopen all source editions, original returned files, review decisions and dispatch mappings, then continue the same workflow in the new private directory.

# GIS merchant tools and typed SDK

The **open311-gis-workspaces** provider operates the same SQLite GIS workspace as the browser and CLI. Its family/configuration key is **open311GISWorkspaces** and its host connection field is **open311GISWorkspaceConnection**. Original source, analyst-return and receiving files are selected through explicit host aliases with pinned file hashes.

The provider uses the maintained merchant host, original release store and retained-file reader. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for the complete source selection and private runtime preparation.

## Select private desks and original files

Initialize the operating and receiving directories with open311-gis init. Create a private connection JSON file with mode 0600:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.open311-gis-host.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "operations": {
      "label": "Municipal GIS operations",
      "directory": "/absolute/private/municipal-gis",
      "inputs": {
        "collection": {
          "label": "Complete original municipal collection",
          "path": "/absolute/handover/municipal-collection.json",
          "sha256": "EXACT_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256",
          "kind": "source",
          "format": "json"
        }
      }
    },
    "received": {
      "label": "Received municipal GIS desk",
      "directory": "/absolute/private/municipal-gis-received",
      "inputs": {}
    }
  }
}
~~~

Replace the source SHA-256 with the hash of the complete original file. Use distinct private directories. Relative paths resolve against the connection file's directory. The configuration permits up to 128 workspace aliases and 128 input aliases per workspace.

Input kind is source, return or workspace. Source and receiving inputs use format json. Analyst return inputs use gpkg, geojson, csv or json. A returned-file alias selects the completed analyst file, its exact hash and kind return; a receiving alias selects the complete GIS workspace JSON and kind workspace.

The merchant tool arguments select these declared aliases. Complete original input bytes are checked against the configured hash at admission. Source import and receiving preserve the original text; GeoPackage returns preserve the original binary bytes.

## Initialize and register the maintained merchant host

Save the original initializer options in a private JSON file:

~~~json
{
  "directory": "/absolute/private/gis-merchant",
  "connection": "/absolute/private/gis-host.json",
  "name": "Municipal GIS handoff"
}
~~~

Invoke the source-owned initializer through the prepared runtime:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  merchant-providers init open311-gis-workspaces \
  --options /absolute/private/gis-setup.json
~~~

The equivalent SDK is initializeGISMerchantWorkspace from open311/gis/mcp-setup.mjs. Pass releaseStore when selecting an existing original SF82 release store. Setup retains the original intent and initializer attempts; repeat the same arguments to recover an interrupted setup.

Generate the client configuration on the actual host that launches the installed merchant:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  merchant-mcp-client-config \
  --config /absolute/private/gis-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --name open311-gis \
  --output /absolute/private/gis-mcp-client.json
~~~

The maintained generator records the actual absolute Node executable and prepared stdio source. Apply that server entry through the MCP client's existing configuration workflow. To preserve other servers, use the generator's --merge option with the existing client JSON, select an unused server name and write a new output file.

The direct terminal transport uses merchant-mcp-stdio --config /absolute/private/gis-merchant/merchant-mcp.json through the same runtime-install run command. A receiving host prepares its delivered runtime and generates its own host-local client entry.

## Complete operating surface

| Tool suffix after merchant_open311_gis_ | Result |
| --- | --- |
| workspaces | Configured desks and original input aliases |
| status | Workspace ID, revision, saved record counts, recent operations and downloads |
| records | Paged source, handoff, return, decision or dispatch summaries |
| input | Original configured file purpose, format, size and hash |
| inspect_source | Complete source description and saved report choices |
| import_source | Retain the exact source file and selected original records |
| handoff_create | Save a named source selection, filters, analyst defaults and optional predecessor |
| source_rows | Search and page original imported rows |
| handoff_info | Saved definition, source coverage and operating row page |
| row | One complete request, source versions and accepted analyst fields |
| return_import | Retain a complete analyst file and its proposals/conflicts/missing rows |
| return_info | Page proposals, conflicts, missing keys or review decisions |
| decision_save | Explicitly accept/reject proposals and save the next handoff edition |
| dispatch_create | Save reviewed action=dispatch rows and destination column mapping |
| dispatch_info | Dispatch identity, destination, mapping, coverage and row page |
| operation | Recover the original saved action result |
| receive | Receive the complete GIS workspace into an empty selected desk |
| file_read | Complete source/return/analyst/dispatch/workspace/operation bytes |
| file_release | Release a retained reader |

Record and row pages require the observed expectedRevision. Follow nextOffset until null. Page limits are 1–100 for the merchant transport; browser/API pages support 1–1000. Large complete source and returned files use the retained-file interface.

Each mutation requires requestId and expectedRevision. Read status before a new action. Recover an uncertain action using its original request ID and input; original results remain available after independent receiving. The operation view replaces large input bodies with their byte/hash manifests and host alias selection; kind operation downloads the complete saved input and result. A receiving operation stores originalFile {sha256,bytes} and incomingPackageSha256 in its input descriptor. Its original source files, analyst uploads and complete record/history transfer remain in the receiving workspace; successive receiving operations keep that descriptor compact.

## Typed transport adapter

The SDK adapts an existing merchant callTool function. For an application importing the installed package:

~~~js
import { Open311GISMerchantClient } from
  '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-gis/client';
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const desk = new Open311GISMerchantClient(
  (name, args) => merchantTransport.callTool({ name, arguments: args }),
  'operations',
);

const state = await desk.status();
const source = await desk.importSource({
  input: 'collection',
  expectedSha256: originalCollectionFileSha256,
  requestId: 'gis-source-intake-001',
  expectedRevision: state.revision,
});
const handoff = await desk.createHandoff({
  requestId: 'gis-handoff-001',
  expectedRevision: source.revision,
  definition: {
    name: 'Municipal GIS allocation',
    sourceIds: [source.source.id],
    defaults: { action: 'review' },
  },
});
const file = await desk.downloadFile({
  kind: 'gpkg',
  handoffId: handoff.handoff.id,
  expectedRevision: handoff.revision,
});
await writeFile('/absolute/handover/municipal-analyst.gpkg', file.bytes, {
  flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600,
});
~~~

After the edited file is selected in a host return alias, use importReturn with its alias/hash, original handoff ID and analyst. Page returned changes with returned, then call decide with the explicit current handoff ID, reviewer and accepted/rejected proposal IDs. CreateDispatch accepts the same definition as the browser/CLI, including destination column names.

DownloadFile verifies each chunk's exact byte count, stable file manifest, complete SHA-256 and terminal offset. An onChunk async sink streams large files to the caller's output. The original selection, expected hash and offset identify continuation. The maintained retained reader controls the snapshot; a later live workspace change leaves that already retained file selection intact.

## Receiving and provider ownership

The receiving input alias points to a complete exported GIS workspace JSON. Use receive with its exact hash and a new stable receiving request ID while the destination desk is empty. The workspace importer reconstructs original source selections, analyst comparisons, decision lineage and dispatch derivation before committing.

The provider opens its selected SQLite handles lazily and drains admitted operations on close. It releases its own retained readers and database handles. The independent browser process continues operating the same saved workspace.

The full installed product includes the original source collector and reporting workbench, so a receiving operator can import later source editions, refresh the current GIS handoff, review new analyst changes and prepare the next complete dispatch.

# Geographic handoff workspace

This workspace carries complete municipal case sources through GIS editing, review and a saved dispatch. Open its saved directory through the installed **Open311 geographic handoff** Application. Each source import, analyst return, decision and dispatch becomes a saved edition.

## Bring the original source

In **Original sources**, choose the complete JSON export from an Open311 collection or the full Open311 reporting workspace. A reporting workspace carries the report and its original collection sources. When it contains several reports, select the intended report before importing.

The source inspection shows the selected source type, size and row count. Give the edition a useful name and choose **Import source edition**. The saved source panel retains the original uploaded file, the selected report identity, publisher attribution and the collection's coverage. **Download original source** returns the uploaded bytes.

Collections selected by created date and collections selected by updated date keep their original selection. Cases appearing in more than one imported source remain connected to their original observations.

## Create an analyst's working edition

In **Analyst packages**, name the handoff and choose its source editions. An optional selection narrows it by source text, native status, service code or valid point location. An initial assignment can include a team, asset, work order, priority, due date, action and note.

Choose **Create saved handoff**. The saved edition offers:

| Download | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GeoPackage | A complete geographic editing file for a GIS application such as QGIS. |
| GeoJSON | WGS84 point features and the source/assignment attributes. |
| CSV | A tabular operating file retaining the stable case identity and source version. |
| Editable JSON | The original structured analyst return format. |
| Report | A complete readable handoff report with source coverage. |

Use the stable case key and retained source columns already in the file. A GeoPackage's integer feature ID is local to that file; the case key connects edits to the original source.

Rows without a valid point remain part of the handoff and exports. Coordinates use longitude followed by latitude. The original source record, including any separately supplied projected coordinates, remains attached to the row.

## Inspect geography and cases

**Map and cases** shows the selected handoff edition. Search locates cases by the server's case text selection, and **Previous** / **Next** move through the complete matching population.

The coordinate overview plots locations on the current page against their retained longitude and latitude. Select a point or case ID to open its description, original source status notes, original and current geometry, source observation history, assignment and report context.

Case selections remain selected across pages of the same handoff. **Clear selection** clears the current set. Every handoff export contains the complete saved handoff; search and pagination control the working view.

## Receive an analyst's edits

The analyst can propose a point location and changes to these assignment fields:

| Field | Intended content |
| --- | --- |
| Assigned team | The team that should handle the case. |
| Asset ID | The receiving system's asset reference. |
| Work order ID | The receiving system's work order reference. |
| Priority | The operator's priority label. |
| Action | `review`, `dispatch`, `defer` or `dismiss`. |
| Due date | A calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form. |
| Analyst note | The context accompanying the proposed action. |

In **Returned edits**, select the exact handoff edition the analyst received. Enter the analyst and return names, choose the complete returned GeoPackage, GeoJSON, CSV or editable JSON file, and choose **Receive proposed edits**.

The workspace retains the entire uploaded file and separates proposed edits from file conflicts. A changed original source column, unknown/duplicate case key or invalid coordinate remains available for correction. Rows absent from the return stay in the original handoff. **Download original returned file** recovers the complete received file.

Browser intake accepts files up to 64 MiB. The installed command line supports the larger operating intake documented in the product guide.

## Review against the current source

For each proposed case change, the review shows the original baseline and analyst value. Choose **Accept proposal**, **Reject proposal** or **Leave pending**. A proposal groups that case's changed fields; its saved original baseline travels with it.

Choose the current target handoff edition from the same series, enter the reviewer and review note, then choose **Save reviewed edition**. The system checks the original source version and the current values of the proposed fields before accepting the change. A concurrent source or field change returns the specific conflict for review.

The decision creates a new immutable handoff edition. Rejected proposals and earlier files remain in history. Unselected proposals remain available for later review. Saved accepted and rejected proposals show their reviewer and time. **Accept remaining proposals** selects only the proposals that still await a decision. The original uploaded file is available alongside every saved return.

For a fresh source period or an updated source capture, import the complete new source and use **Continue with new sources** from the earlier handoff. The successor keeps the same series and identifies changed original case versions for a fresh review.

## Prepare reviewed dispatch

In **Reviewed dispatch**, choose a reviewed handoff, name the package and identify the receiving team or system. The default selection includes the rows with an accepted analyst decision setting the action to `dispatch`. A selected-case package uses the explicit selections from that exact handoff.

An optional destination column mapping uses the product's known field names. Original case identity and source-version columns remain part of the output. The product's command-line guide documents the canonical field names and complete mapping format.

Choose **Prepare saved dispatch**. Download GeoPackage, GeoJSON, CSV, structured JSON or the readable report. Each export contains the complete saved dispatch, its source coverage and retained decision links.

## Transfer the complete workspace

**Save workspace** downloads the full editable geographic workspace. It includes every original collection/report file, handoff edition, analyst upload, proposal, review decision, dispatch and saved action.

The receiving operator opens an empty initialized GIS workspace through Applications or the installed command line. In **Open a handover**, choose the complete geographic workspace JSON and select **Receive and open original workspace**. Receiving preserves the original workspace identity and its source and review history. The saved directory can be reopened for continued work.

Use the complete workspace with the destination's dispatch exports when handing over operations. A specific GeoPackage or CSV is useful for field work; the workspace retains the complete editable history.

## Recover an interrupted action

A mutation carries one saved request identity and the workspace edition it was based on. When a connection interrupts the response, the browser retains the original request and offers **Find saved result**. This reads the saved native operation.

If the native workspace has no saved result, **Resume original action** sends that same request identity and exact original input. A saved success is recovered without creating another source, return or decision. If another operator has advanced the selected edition, refresh and review the new current state before issuing a new action.

The browser retains available form drafts and pending proposal choices in its local storage, bound to the selected saved directory. A receiving action keeps that same recovery binding when it adopts the incoming workspace identity. The workspace database and complete handover retain the actual saved source and operating history.

# Boston geographic customer commissioning

This operating program takes the original Boston collection and service report through the installed GIS browser, an editable GeoPackage, reviewed dispatch, a second browser receiving desk, the installed CLI, and the merchant client. It saves the full operating workspaces and usable dispatch files.

The input is the completed original Boston collection/reporting operation in `operations/open311-boston-8e5f-20261012/`. Its four source files contain the original 84 created cases, 21 updated cases, empty updated window, and combined 104-case report. The geographic program imports every original byte and uses the original case identities and coordinates. Its three analyst assignments are explicitly labelled internal commissioning work.

## Operating sequence

1. Import all four complete original files through the geographic browser and retain their source history. Create a 104-case collection handoff and a separate 104-case handoff from the selected service report.
2. Read the map and both case pages, find a real case by its original identifier, and open its original source status note.
3. Download the complete GeoPackage. Use native SQLite to assign three actual source rows in the editable analyst fields.
4. Receive the edited package through the browser. Accept one proposal, reject one, reload the desk, and finish the remaining review. The saved decision history and pending reviewer choice survive reopening.
5. Select the two accepted dispatch cases across the 100-row page boundary. Save the destination column mapping and download complete GeoPackage, GeoJSON, CSV, JSON and HTML dispatch files.
6. Download the editable workspace. Receive it into a second initialized browser desk. Interrupt the HTTP response after the real server commit, then reload and recover the same saved operation. Continue the received handoff.
7. Close the browser and native desks, reopen the saved SQLite workspace independently, and receive the resulting complete file again through the installed CLI.
8. Open the original configured merchant integration, page all 104 cases in groups of 17, download the complete workspace and mapped dispatch file, and recover the original receiving operation.

The receiving operations keep a compact incoming-file descriptor alongside the original records and source files. The saved handover sizes show the actual change across each receiving hop.

## Delivered files

The private output contains the four complete original inputs; original and edited GeoPackages; five destination dispatch formats; the complete sender, receiving, reopened, CLI and merchant workspace JSON files; the independently saved SQLite workspace directories; the merchant host configuration; six browser screenshots; and `journey.json`.

`OPEN311_GIS_PHASE` reports a completed actual operating step. `OPEN311_GIS_COMPLETE` reports the final state and output directory. The program exits nonzero on a failed operation and keeps the available work and original error in the same private output.

The source is paired with the GIS product merged in public PR2453 and standalone PR404. Run results belong to the executing host and are saved with the actual source edition in `journey.json`.
